title: US markets closed — Christmas Day 2028 (a Monday closure, with no Christmas Eve early close in the NYSE's own 2028 footnote list)
source: NEWS: nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200 after its 302, 109,180 bytes; needs curl -L, and its holiday data parses as JSON-ish '"text":"..."' cells rather than HTML table markup). The page states 'All NYSE markets observe U.S. holidays as listed below for 2026, 2027, and 2028'; the Christmas Day row parses as 'Friday, December 25****' / 'Friday, December 24 (Christmas Day observed)' / 'Monday, December 25', so the 2028 cell carries NO footnote marker at all — footnote **** applies only to 2026 and reads 'Each market will close early at 1:00 p.m. (1:15 p.m. for eligible options) on Thursday, December 24, 2026', naming no 2028 date. Friday 2028-12-22 is therefore a full 09:30-16:00 ET session on the exchange's own published grid. Independently reproduced by statute and weekday arithmetic: 5 U.S.C. 6103 (uscode.house.gov, HTTP 200, 170,863 bytes) fixes Christmas Day on December 25, and 2028-12-25 is a Monday. Filed estimate on the two counts every sibling closure entry records: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an exchange operator's own hours page (open issue #2552, which measures 37 of 37 closure entries stuck at estimate for exactly this reason), and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The OCC expiration calendar publishes 2025-2027 only and SIFMA's US panel runs out at January 1 2028, so neither corroborating source that exists for christmas-market-closure-2027-12-24 is available here — the 2028 date rests on the NYSE grid plus statute. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of thanksgiving-market-closure-2028-11-23, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED by the thanksgiving-market-closure-2028-11-23 initial research (2026-09-09), whose mandatory adjacency sweep was run mechanically over all 942 tracked entries (566 canonical, 376 proposals) and found the plus-or-minus-60-day corridor around 2028-11-23 to contain exactly two things besides the proposer itself: presidential-election-2028-11-07 at D-16 and fed-board-closure-2028-11-10 at D-13. Everything after 2028-11-24 was blank — that date and its own half-day sibling were the two furthest-out entries on the entire calendar. This is the next structural date past the frontier, at D+32, and it comes off the same primary fetch that dated the proposer. WHY IT MATTERS TO THE PROPOSER AND NOT MERELY AS BOOKKEEPING: the proposer's one measured finding is that the post-Thanksgiving repricing displacement does NOT reach a five-Thursday November, and the mechanism it declines to rule out is month-end and year-end flow stacking onto the displaced Monday. Any later attribution of December 2028 tape behaviour has to know that 12-25 is shut and that — unusually — 12-22 is NOT an early close, because the 2026 pattern (a Thursday Christmas Eve half day) does not repeat when Christmas lands on a Monday. ONE PROPOSAL, NOT A COLUMN DUMP: the NYSE grid read this session also names seven other 2028 US holidays and a July 3 2028 early close, none of which is adjacent to the proposer; they are deliberately left unproposed rather than harvested, so this row stands on corridor relevance and not on the convenience of having the page open. NOTHING TRADEABLE IS CLAIMED: symbols is empty, impact is low, no house playbook is calendar-keyed (re-grepped this session, 0 hits in both docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md and docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md), and estimate widens caution and licenses no entry.
